    StartersMainsSweetsDrinks
    StartersKerim Bey's sesame simitTwisted sesame bread rings glazed with grape molasses, with fetaHow to make it350g plain flour7g dried yeast1 tsp sugar1 tsp salt220ml warm water2 tbsp olive oil80ml grape molasses or date syrup80ml water, for the dip120g sesame seeds200g fetaMix the flour, yeast, sugar, salt, warm water and oil and knead for 10 minutes until smooth.Cover and leave to rise for an hour until doubled.Heat the oven to 220°C. Divide into 8, roll each into two thin ropes, twist them together and join the ends into a ring.Dip each ring in the molasses mixed with the water, then press into the sesame seeds on both sides.Rest on lined trays for 15 minutes.Bake for 15 minutes until deep golden.Cool slightly and serve with the feta.Bosphorus stuffed musselsBlack mussels stuffed with spiced rice, pine nuts and currants, steamed and served with lemonHow to make it150g medium grain rice1 onion, finely diced3 tbsp olive oil2 tbsp pine nuts2 tbsp currants1 tsp ground allspice1/2 tsp ground cinnamon1 tsp tomato paste1 tsp sugar1/2 tsp salt1/4 tsp black pepper450ml water1 tbsp dill, chopped1 tsp dried mint24 large black mussels2 lemons, cut into wedgesSoak the rice in hot water for 20 minutes, then drain.Scrub and debeard the mussels, throwing out any that stay open when tapped.Fry the onion and pine nuts in the oil for 8 minutes until golden. Add the rice, allspice, cinnamon, tomato paste, sugar, salt, pepper, currants and 250ml of the water, cover and simmer for 10 minutes until the water is absorbed but the rice is still firm. Stir in the dill and mint.Spread the rice on a tray to cool.Slide a small knife into each mussel at the flat edge and open it without separating the shells. Fill with a spoonful of rice and close.Pack the mussels into a pot, pour in the rest of the water, weigh down with a plate, cover and steam for 20 minutes.Cool for 10 minutes and serve with the lemon wedges.MainsOrient Express dining car solePan-fried sole in nutty brown butter with lemon, capers and parsley, new potatoes and green beansHow to make it600g new potatoes250g green beans, trimmed600g sole or flounder filletssalt and pepper, to taste50g plain flour2 tbsp vegetable oil100g butter2 lemons1 tbsp capers, rinsed2 tbsp parsley, choppedBoil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15 minutes. Drain and keep warm.Blanch the beans in boiling water for 3 minutes and drain.Season the fish with salt and pepper and dust lightly with the flour.Fry the fillets in the oil and 20g of the butter for 2 minutes a side, in batches. Keep warm on plates.Wipe the pan, add the rest of the butter and cook until it smells nutty and turns light brown. Add the juice of 1 lemon, the capers and parsley.Spoon the butter over the plates and serve with the potatoes, beans and the other lemon in wedges.Kerim Bey's camp supper lamb shishThe night at the camp outside Istanbul, before the shooting startsHow to make it800g lamb leg, diced2 tsp sweet paprika1 tsp ground cumin3 tbsp olive oil1 lemon1 green capsicum1 red onion250g coarse bulgur20g butter200g Greek yoghurt3 tomatoes1 Lebanese cucumber1 parsleyToss the lamb with the paprika, cumin, 2 tbsp of the oil, half the lemon juice and salt. Thread onto skewers with chunks of capsicum and onion.Fry the bulgur in the butter for 1 minute, add 500ml water and salt, cover and simmer for 15 minutes, then rest for 5.Dice the tomatoes and cucumber and mix with chopped parsley, the rest of the oil and lemon.Grill the skewers on a very hot grill for 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until charred.Serve on the pilaf with yoghurt and the salad.SweetsGrand Bazaar rose Turkish delightRosewater Turkish delight with pistachios, cut into cubes and rolled in icing sugarHow to make it1 tsp neutral oil, for the tin600g caster sugar800ml water1 tbsp lemon juice100g cornflour, for the jelly1 tsp cream of tartar1 1/2 tbsp rosewaterpink food colouring, a few drops50g shelled pistachios3 tbsp icing sugar3 tbsp cornflour, for dustingOil a 20cm square tin and line it with baking paper.Boil the sugar, 200ml of the water and the lemon juice to 115°C on a sugar thermometer.In a second heavy pan whisk the cornflour for the jelly and the cream of tartar into the remaining 600ml water and cook, stirring, until it becomes a thick paste.Slowly whisk the hot syrup into the paste. Simmer very gently for an hour, stirring often, until pale gold and very thick.Stir in the rosewater, colouring and pistachios and pour into the tin.Leave uncovered at room temperature to set overnight.Mix the icing sugar and cornflour for dusting. Cut into cubes with an oiled knife and toss in the mix.DrinksKerim Bey's raki and pomegranateAniseed raki clouded over ice with pomegranate juice, lemon, soda, mint and pomegranate seedsHow to make it2 cups ice120ml raki30ml lemon juice20ml sugar syrup200ml pomegranate juice, chilled200ml soda water, chilled4 mint sprigs2 tbsp pomegranate seedsFill 4 glasses with ice.Add the raki, lemon juice and sugar syrup and stir until it turns cloudy.Top with the pomegranate juice and soda.Finish with a mint sprig and a few pomegranate seeds.
